summary: v6 cache-stability (append-only `lean` vs re-ranked `search`): STRUCTURAL NULL — not runnable as framed; no trials run (would only confirm parity at cost). Premise is false under this harness: (a) one `claude -p` run is ONE multi-turn session WITH a warm reused cache (cache_read climbs monotonically turn-to-turn — so a cache to break does exist), but (b) BOTH lean and search inject the knowledge tool-result exactly ONCE per session (verified in transcripts: 1 call, several runs 0), and MCP tool-results are append-only by construction — neither re-ranks per turn; (c) a mid-session search_knowledge call provably does NOT invalidate the cache (v5-grounded-on-2: cache_read keeps climbing after the search call). Cache invalidation needs earlier-prefix content rewritten on a later turn; the orchestrator only appends tool-results at the prefix END, so it has NO lever to break (or, vs strawman, to 'save') the cache via injection stability. Under headless `claude -p` the Claude Code harness owns prompt layout/cache_control; orchestrator has no prefix slot. To exercise it would need a NEW harness component owning a pinned prompt-prefix slot recomputed each turn (multi-consult spec + re-ranked top-k digest in fixed position) — bounded by the task's own CRITICAL CONSTRAINT. This explains a facet of prior v2–v5 parity: orchestrator injection is always append-only for both arms, so injection-stability is a non-lever.
